newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's MFK bank expects Norilsk sale Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Russia's MFK bank expects Norilsk sale Tuesday.

text.p: Russia's Bank MFK, the investment bank affiliate of commercial bank Uneximbank, said it expected the results of a tender for 38 percent of mining giant Norilsk Nickel to be announced on Tuesday, although the announcement could be delayed by several hours to around 6 p.m. local time (1400 GMT).

"The (tender) committee will meet tomorrow at around noon, and we will discuss the situation...We expect to announce the results (of the tender) by six o'clock," said Oleg Sapozhnikov, spokesman of Bank MFK, known as IFCI in English.
Doubts were raised when Russian news agencies quoted government sources as saying Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had ordered the sale be suspended.

A senior Uneximbank official said that Chernomyrdin's instruction did in fact exist, but that it was not enough to halt the sale. Bids in the auction were closed last Friday, and the results were to have been announced at noon local time (0800 GMT) on Tuesday.

The fate of the tender is still unclear, because contrary to Uneximbank's statement, Federal Property Fund chairman Igor Lipkin said earlier that if Chernomyrdin made such an order, the fund would stop the sale.

Uneximbank has had control of the Norilsk stake, which represents 51 percent of voting shares, since 1995, and was widely tipped to win Tuesday's auction. But public and political furore over the terms of the sale may have prompted Chernomyrdin into action.
